0 # html-to-markdown A robust html-to-markdown converter that transforms HTML (including entire webpages) into clean, readable Markdown. It supports complex formatting, configurable options, and extensibility via plugins. This repository provides the user-facing documentation and examples of how the converter behaves. Implementation details (source code, build files, CI, and developer guides) have been removed to focus on what the tool does and how to use it. Usage (generic): - CLI: html-to-markdown [OPTIONS] - Example options: --input , --output , --preserve-tags , --wrap-links - Hosted: Try the hosted demo and API at https://html-to-markdown.com Input: HTML content (string, file, or URL). Output: Markdown (stdout or file). Examples: - Convert a single HTML file to Markdown (generic): html-to-markdown --input page.html --output page.md - Convert a website and write to stdout (generic): html-to-markdown --input https://example.com Notes: - The converter handles lists, blockquotes, inline code, code blocks, images, links, tables, and smart escaping of special characters. - For advanced options and integrations, consult the hosted demo or API documentation at https://html-to-markdown.com License: This project is provided under the terms in the LICENSE file. --- ## Escaping Some characters have a special meaning in markdown. For example, the character "\*" can be used for lists, emphasis and dividers. By placing a backlash before that character (e.g. "\\\*") you can "escape" it. Then the character will render as a raw "\*" without the _"markdown meaning"_ applied. But why is "escaping" even necessary? ```md Paragraph 1 - Paragraph 2 ``` The markdown above doesn't seem that problematic. But "Paragraph 1" (with only one hyphen below) will be recognized as a _setext heading_. ```html

Paragraph 1

Paragraph 2

``` A well-placed backslash character would prevent that... ```md Paragraph 1 \- Paragraph 2 ``` --- How to configure escaping? Depending on the `EscapeMode` option, the markdown output is going to be different. ```go conv := converter.NewConverter( converter.WithEscapeMode("smart"), // default converter.WithPlugins( // ... ) ) ``` Lets try it out with this HTML input: | | | | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | input | `

fake **bold** and real bold

` | | | | | | **With EscapeMode "smart"** | | output | `fake \*\*bold\*\* and real **bold**` | | rendered | fake \*\*bold\*\* and real **bold** | | | | | | **With EscapeMode "disabled"** | | output | `fake **bold** and real **bold**` | | rendered | fake **bold** and real **bold** | With **smart** escaping, we get some escape characters (the backlash "\\") but it renders correctly. With escaping **disabled**, the fake and real bold can't be distinguished in the markdown. That means it is both going to render as bold. --- So now you know the purpose of escaping. However, if you encounter some content where the escaping breaks, you can manually disable it. But please also open an issue! --- # Security Policy ## Reporting a Vulnerability Please report (suspected) security vulnerabilities to johannes@joina.de with the subject _"Security html-to-markdown"_ and you will receive a response within 48 hours. --- MIT License Copyright (c) 2018 Johannes Kaufmann Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions: The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software. content.content: 0 # html2markdown - convert html to markdown [version dev] Convert HTML to Markdown. Even works with entire websites! ## Basics By default the "Commonmark" Plugin will be enabled. You can customize the options, for example changing the appearance of bold with --opt-strong-delimiter="__" Other Plugins can also be enabled. For example "GitHub Flavored Markdown" (GFM) extends Commonmark with more features. ## Relative / Absolute Links Use --domain="https://example.com" to convert *relative* links to *absolute* links. The same also works for images. ## Escaping Some characters have a special meaning in markdown. The library escapes these — if necessary. See the documentation for more info. ## Security Once you convert this markdown *back* to HTML you need to be careful of malicious content. # The "  \n  \n  \n" (indented blank lines) is NOT collapsed by re.sub(r'\n{3,}', ...)
# because each line has "  " (2 spaces) which makes the "line" non-empty

# Fix: in _list_item, before splitting into lines, collapse multiple blank lines
# The blank lines in the li content should only have ONE blank line between paragraphs
# This needs to happen BEFORE the line-by-line processing

# Also: the trailing "\n\n" from _list is fine - after strip('\n'), it goes away
# But the extra "  \n  \n  \n" (from multiple blank lines in first li) doesn't strip

# The fix is to collapse multiple blank lines in _list_item AFTER strip('\n'):
# inner = inner.strip('\n')
# inner = re.sub(r'\n\n+', '\n\n', inner)  <- collapse multiple \n\n to one
# But this won't work for "  \n  \n  \n" because each line has "  " content!

# Better fix: in _convert_li_content, after generating the content,
# collapse runs of empty/whitespace-only lines to single empty line

# Actually the cleanest fix is to strip the inner content more aggressively:
# After strip('\n') on inner content, replace runs of blank-ish lines with one blank line
# A "blank-ish" line is one that's all whitespace

python3 -c "
import re
inner = 'para1\n\n\n\npara2'
# The issue: strip('\n') gives us this
# Then the multi-block handler sees ['para1', '', '', '', 'para2']
# Fix: collapse consecutive blank lines in the stripped inner content
lines = inner.split('\n')
collapsed = []
prev_blank = False
for line in lines:
    if line.strip() == '':
        if not prev_blank:
            collapsed.append('')
        prev_blank = True
    else:
        collapsed.append(line)
        prev_blank = False
print('Collapsed lines:', collapsed)
"

# Fix approach 1: strip all trailing whitespace (including spaces) from result

# But this would break results that legitimately have trailing spaces before \n (BR elements)

# Fix approach 2: strip trailing whitespace-only lines from the result
# Like: remove any lines at the end that contain only whitespace

# Fix approach 3: don't generate the trailing " " in the first place
# In _convert_node for '#text', check if parent is root (block context)
# and return '' for whitespace-only text

# Let me go with Fix approach 3 but at a higher level:
# In convert(), after generating the full result, strip trailing whitespace
# but preserve "  " (exactly 2 spaces) before newlines

python3 -c "
import re
result = 'Hello \*world\*\n\n \n'
# Remove trailing whitespace-only lines from the end
lines = result.split('\n')
while lines and lines[-1].strip() == '':
    lines.pop()
result = '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'
print(repr(result))
"

        result = result.strip('\\n')
        # Remove trailing whitespace-only lines (but keep the final newline)
        lines = result.split('\\n')
        while lines and lines[-1].strip() == '' and not lines[-1].endswith('  '):
            lines.pop()
        result = '\\n'.join(lines) + '\\n'
        return result"""

        result = '\\n'.join(cleaned) + '\\n'

def build_table_grid(all_rows_raw):
    """Build a 2D grid from raw rows, respecting colspan/rowspan."""
    if not all_rows_raw:
        return []
    
    # First, determine approximate dimensions
    max_cols = max(sum(c.get('colspan', 1) for c in row) for row in all_rows_raw)
    n_rows = len(all_rows_raw)
    
    # Build grid: None = empty/unset, '' = filled by span
    grid = [[None] * max_cols for _ in range(n_rows)]
    
    for row_idx, raw_row in enumerate(all_rows_raw):
        col_idx = 0
        for cell in raw_row:
            # Skip filled positions
            while col_idx < max_cols and grid[row_idx][col_idx] is not None:
                col_idx += 1
            
            if col_idx >= max_cols:
                break
            
            colspan = cell.get('colspan', 1)
            rowspan = cell.get('rowspan', 1)
            content = cell.get('content', '')
            
            # Fill the grid positions
            for r in range(rowspan):
                for c in range(colspan):
                    r2 = row_idx + r
                    c2 = col_idx + c
                    if r2 < n_rows and c2 < max_cols:
                        if r == 0 and c == 0:
                            grid[r2][c2] = content
                        else:
                            grid[r2][c2] = ''  # span-filled
            
            col_idx += colspan
    
    # Convert None to '' (unfilled cells)
    result = []
    for row in grid:
        result.append([c if c is not None else '' for c in row])
    
    return result
